summary: New Testament Lectionary for the entire year (Jerusalem rite)
fol: Foliation in Syriac letters in the top margin of each recto side added by a later hand. The actual sequence suggests that one folio preceding f. 1 is missing. The small fragment originally belonged to f. 1 (features Mt. 5:22).
coll: Quires 1-2: 2x12 (24), Quire 3: 1x8 (29b), folio 30 is a singleton, Quires 4-5: 2x8 (46), Quire 6: 1x12 (58), Quire 7: 1x10 (66), Quire 8: 1x8 (74), Quire 9: 1x10 (84), Quire 10: 1x8 (91), Quire 11: 1x8 (98), Quire 12: 1x12 (110), folio 110a is a singleton, folio 110b is the paste-down in the back cover

location.repository: St. Catherine's Monastery of the Sinai

note.value: Foliation in pencil in upper or lower margin, which sometimes includes numbered folios with the suffix a or b (e.g., f. 63, followed by f. 63a and f. 63b)
The original first five folios of the codex are fragmentary, not numbered, and are not considered here; the sixth folio in the codex is numbered 1, followed here
Foliation in Syriac letters in the top margin of each recto side added by a later hand. The actual sequence suggests that one folio preceding f. 1 is missing.
No visible quire signatures. The quire composition cannot be determined from the images. Nonetheless, the manuscript appears complete, with only one folio missing.
Leather front and back covers; leather spine with reinforced fabric. Front cover detached; back cover attached; spine partially detached.
Many folios exhibit significant damage, occasionally leaving only a narrow strip of the inner margin intact.
Until ca. f. 32, spine slants outward, resulting in curled folios

Judging from the indications of the scribe (f. 88r–v, 110r), the actual lectionary is the second (companion) volume of the original set of two. The first volume, covering the readings for the feasts, has not survived.
Palimpsest throughout with underwriting in CPA, Syriac and Armenian

program.label: Sinai Palimpsests Project
program.description: Imaged and studied as part of the Sinai Palimpsests Project (2011–2016), a collaboration between St. Catherine’s Monastery of the Sinai, the Early Manuscripts Electronic Library, and UCLA Library, funded by the Arcadia Fund and the Ahmanson Foundation. The project used multispectral imaging and scholarly analysis to recover and document erased and obscured texts in palimpsest manuscripts from the monastery’s collection.
